first.rationale: Two independent consolidated memories (31 and 86) both support that reducing friction in signup/onboarding durably lifts activation and completion, which directly targets the two internal metrics currently declining (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%). This is a safer, more sustainable lever than reacting to competitor pricing: promotional_pricing (memory_73) could win short-term price-sensitive SMB share but risks margin erosion and a race-to-bottom that undermines 'sustainable long-term qualified revenue,' so I want to verify its original record before ever committing to it, and I'm verifying memory_86 to make sure it isn't simply a restatement of memory_31 inflating apparent evidential weight. Enterprise, referral, and activation-messaging levers don't address the acute quarter-over-quarter declines as directly. Given onboarding changes touch top-of-funnel lead composition, there's some risk of attracting lower-quality signups, so I flag downstream value risk and keep the test at standard scale rather than broad rollout, preserving the possibility that verification of the archived records changes the plan.
